title: Headroom probe & throttle timeline extract — 2025-12-16
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an ad-hoc data extract used for the 2025-12-15 capacity incident postmortem. The goal is to produce a compact, audit-friendly timeline (waterfall) showing the interplay of request surge, headroom probes, queue depth, and throttles across regions and GPU pools.

Scope & time window:
- Incident window: 2025-12-15T02:10Z -> 2025-12-15T04:50Z (primary spike)
- Extract range used here: 2025-12-15T00:00Z -> 2025-12-15T06:00Z (to capture pre/post trends)
- Granularity: 1-minute aggregates (rolled up for main timeline), 10s sample for anomaly slices.

Data sources & joins (quick):
- request_events (kafka topic sink): request_id, region, pool_id, route, created_at, start_time, finish_time, status, tokens_generated
- gpu_telemetry_minute: pool_id, region, minute_bucket, util_pct, queued_requests, avg_latency_ms, headroom_pct
- throttle_actions: action_id, pool_id, minute_bucket, throttle_type (rate_limit | queue_drop | soft_limit), policy_id
- kv_cache_pressure: pool_id, minute_bucket, kv_hit_rate, kv_memory_bytes
- autoscaler_probes: probe_id, pool_id, minute_bucket, probe_result (ok | warn | fail), requested_burst

Key metrics computed in this extract (column definitions):
- minute_bucket: ISO minute timestamp (e.g. 2025-12-15T02:12:00Z)
- inbound_rps: requests/sec observed in the minute (sum(requests) / 60)
- avg_gpu_util: weighted average GPU util pct for pool in minute
- queued: max queued_requests reported in the minute
- p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile request completion latency observed in minute
- headroom_pct: 100 - (util_pct) as reported by telemetry (approx free capacity)
- throttle_count: count of throttle_actions in minute_bucket
- kv_hit_rate: avg kv hit rate in minute (0-1)
- probe_failures: count of autoscaler_probes with probe_result != ok

Representative SQLs used to generate timeline (simplified):
1) 1m timeline per pool
SELECT minute_bucket, pool_id, region, 
  SUM(requests) as total_requests, SUM(requests)/60.0 as inbound_rps, 
  AVG(util_pct) as avg_gpu_util, MAX(queued_requests) as queued,
  approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) as p95_latency_ms,
  AVG(100 - util_pct) as headroom_pct,
  SUM(CASE WHEN throttle_type IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as throttle_count,
  AVG(kv_hit_rate) as kv_hit_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN probe_result!='ok' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as probe_failures
FROM request_agg_minute r
LEFT JOIN gpu_telemetry_minute g USING(minute_bucket, pool_id)
LEFT JOIN throttle_actions t USING(minute_bucket, pool_id)
LEFT JOIN kv_cache_pressure k USING(minute_bucket, pool_id)
LEFT JOIN autoscaler_probes a USING(minute_bucket, pool_id)
WHERE minute_bucket >= '2025-12-15T00:00:00Z' AND minute_bucket < '2025-12-15T06:00:00Z'
GROUP BY minute_bucket, pool_id, region
ORDER BY minute_bucket;

2) Anomaly slice (10s) for labeled spike minutes:
SELECT ts, pool_id, region, requests, queued_requests, util_pct, throttle_type
FROM request_events_realtime r
JOIN gpu_telemetry_10s g ON r.pool_id=g.pool_id AND r.ts_bucket=g.ts_bucket
LEFT JOIN throttle_actions t USING(ts_bucket, pool_id)
WHERE ts >= '2025-12-15T02:10:00Z' and ts <= '2025-12-15T02:25:00Z'
ORDER BY ts
LIMIT 10000;

High level timeline summary (derived from extract):
- 02:09 -> 02:12Z: inbound_rps across us-west-2 pools ramps from 420 -> 1,450 rps (3.4x baseline). KV hit rate falls 0.92 -> 0.61 as burst penetrates cold prefixes.
- 02:12Z: first autoscaler_probe failures observed against pool gpu-p-03 (probe_failures=3 in minute). Headroom_pct drops below 12% on pool gpu-p-03.
- 02:13Z -> 02:20Z: queued jumps from 12 -> 180 requests; p95 latency increases 120ms -> 2,800ms. Throttle actions (soft_limit) start at 02:14 and increase to 72 actions/min by 02:17.
- 02:18Z: controller applies global soft-fallback: route split to lower-cost model variant for 'chat' routes in us-west-2 (manual mitigation). This reduces inbound_rps to affected pools by ~30% over 5 minutes.
- 02:30Z -> 03:10Z: tail plateau as autoscaler scales up 2 extra nodes into pool gpu-p-03 and neighbor pools; headroom_pct recovers from 8% -> 38% over 30m.
- 03:12Z: throttle_count returns to baseline; kv_hit_rate recovers as cache warmed.

Anomalies & signals of interest (from extract):
- KV cache hit-rate collapse correlated with request burst and correlated with a spike in unique prompt prefixes (indicative of a campaign causing cache coldness).
- Autoscaler probe failures precede throttle surge by ~1 minute — probe logic (latency-based health checks) misclassified transient queueing as node failure, slowing scale up.
- Throttle actions were primarily 'soft_limit' (policy p-soft-3) which applies token-rate caps per route; side-effect: aggressive soft-limits increased queue churn (retry behavior) and perpetuated latency.
- Two small pools in us-west-2 (gpu-p-09 and gpu-p-11) showed suboptimal placement: they are in a preemptible cluster with slightly lower available memory; their headroom trended to zero faster than sibling pools.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
1) External traffic spike (campaign/partner) drove a large, high-cardinality request set that bypassed typical cache locality assumptions.
2) Cache coldness increased per-request work and per-token cost, raising util and queueing pressure.
3) Autoscaler probe logic (latency+errors) treated transient queue-induced latency as node unhealthiness, delaying scale-in/out decisions.
4) Throttle policy (soft limits) interacting with client retries amplified queue churn.

Immediate mitigations taken (captured in sheet):
- 02:18Z: manual route-split to lighter model variant for high-volume chat routes (reduced tokens per request).
- 02:22Z: manual override to suspend soft_limit policy p-soft-3 for affected pools (stop aggressive rate-capping).
- 02:25Z: requested manual scale-up to add 2x medium GPUs into gpu-p-03 (24m convergence to 38% headroom).

Quantitative impact summary (rough from extract):
- Peak queued requests across pool group: 1,100 (aggregate across us-west-2)
- Minutes with throttle_count > 20 across region: 18 minutes
- Estimated additional token-cost due to cache coldness during incident: ~18% increase over baseline for the 1h window

Recommended actions (longer-term tracked tasks):
- T1 (priority): Adjust autoscaler probe logic to decouple transient queueing from node-health signal (ticket: JIRA-OPS-2399).
- T2: Add prefix-awareness in our routing/caching layer: mark high-cardinality prefixes and route to warming pooling or pre-warmed caches (ticket: CON-724).
- T3: Revisit soft_limit policy parameters and implement exponential backoff for client guidance to reduce retry spikes (ticket: JIRA-THROTTLE-121).
- T4: Re-evaluate pool placement for preemptible clusters; add headroom throttles to avoid placing critical low-memory models on preemptible nodes (ticket: PLAC-58).
- T5: Add a high-resolution (10s) warmup telemetry dashboard to spot KV-hit regressions earlier.

Notes / open questions (working):
- Who initiated the external traffic (partner id not yet validated) — ticket created to CS for partner outreach.
- Are there model-specific patterns (certain prompt shapes) that correlate with low kv_hit_rate? Need a prompt-hash join analysis.
- Autoscaler probe tuning: quantify false-positive rate for probe failures during queue bursts (need historical comparison).

Appendix A — debugging snippets (copied from analysis):
-- quick join to find top prefixes causing kv miss:
SELECT prefix_hash, COUNT(*) as cnt, AVG(tokens) as avg_tokens
FROM request_events
WHERE minute_bucket between '2025-12-15T02:10:00Z' and '2025-12-15T02:20:00Z'
GROUP BY prefix_hash
ORDER BY cnt desc
LIMIT 50;

-- throttle action rollup by policy
SELECT policy_id, SUM(1) as actions, SUM(CASE WHEN throttle_type='queue_drop' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as drops
FROM throttle_actions
WHERE minute_bucket between '2025-12-15T02:10:00Z' and '2025-12-15T02:25:00Z'
GROUP BY policy_id
ORDER BY actions desc;

Appendix B — export checklist (how this sheet was made):
- Pull minute and 10s telemetry from warehouse (tables: gpu_telemetry_minute, gpu_telemetry_10s)
- Pull request aggregates and events (request_agg_minute, request_events_realtime)
- Pull throttle logs and autoscaler probe logs
- Run above SQLs in datalab, export CSV and pivot as needed

Contact: arjun@redwood.ai (for follow-up on queries or missing joins).

-- End of extract sheet --
